newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan allocates new Haneda slots to airlines.
newsitem.headline: Japan allocates new Haneda slots to airlines.

text.p: The Transport Ministry said on Thursday that it would allocate 13 new slots to Japan Air System Co Ltd (JAS) and 12 new slots to Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) out of 40 new slots at Tokyo's Haneda Airport.
The ministry said in a statement that it would also allocate nine new slots to All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA). New airlines will get a total of six slots, the ministry said.

A third runway is due to open at the Tokyo International Airport at Haneda, which is mainly a domestic airport, later this month but airlines will not be able to use the new slots until July, the ministry said.

In allocating the new slots, the ministry introduced a new system, in line with Japan's overall deregulation, under which airlines are free to decide the destinations of the flights using new slots. Of the 40 new slots, 34 are such free-destination slots, the ministry said.
Previously, the ministry allocated new slots for specific routes planned by airlines.
The destinations for six of ANA's nine new slots have already been decided in an conventional way, the ministry said. None of the six routes are key routes, it said.
Both ANA and JAL said they were not happy about the ministry's decision.

"We are very dissatisfied with the allocation," an ANA spokesman said. "We welcome the introduction of a free-slot system but the number of new slots we will earn is far smaller than we wanted," he said.
A JAL spokesman said that the ministry's decision would not help ease unfairness in the domestic airline business.
Currently ANA has the largest domestic network in Japan, with around a 50 percent share of the Japanese market.
